clue.text: Phone feature increases values

blocks.note: an app is a program that runs on a smartphone
to raise something is to increase it

explanation.surface: A new smartphone function pushes up prices or worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Values' reads as a plural noun after 'increases', but it is a verb meaning assesses the worth of.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise something is to estimate its worth, which is what valuing it means.

clue.text: Very pale, like a bird?

blocks.note: 'as' means 'like', in a comparison
a hen is a female bird, typically a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone looks white-faced, perhaps as pale as a feathered creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'like a bird' as two words joined: AS + HEN makes ASHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face grey-white like ash, drained of colour from shock or illness.

clue.text: Piano finale up in the air

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
a finale is the ending of a piece or show

explanation.surface: The last movement of a piano work is still undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pending is awaiting a decision, as an unresolved matter is said to be up in the air.

clue.text: Choir members in cathedral to sing

indicators.note: the wanted letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Singers in a cathedral choir are ready to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choir members in cathedral' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the signal: cathedrAL TO Sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos are singers of the part below soprano, one of the standard voice sections in a choir.

clue.text: Terminal position in society?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stop where trains or buses end their journey
second meaning: one's rank or standing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' looks like an adjective describing the position (final), but it is a noun on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway terminus is a station, and one's social rank is also called one's station in life.

clue.text: Dramatist playing polo and chess

indicators.note: playing with something means moving it about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playwright spends leisure time on horseback games and at the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was an ancient Greek tragedian, author of Oedipus Rex, so a writer of plays.

clue.text: Second-rate auction item — dry piece of writing

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to dry wet ink on a written page

blocks.note: B grade means second class
each item sold at an auction is a numbered lot

explanation.surface: A mediocre item at a sale is described as a dull piece of prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry piece of writing' suggests a boring text; here it is an instruction, to dry what has been written.
explanation.definitionFit: To blot is to soak up excess ink with blotting paper, drying a freshly written page.

clue.text: Advantageous purchase provides pub with profit

blocks.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Buying wisely gives a pub owner a healthy return.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something bought cheaply for its worth, a purchase that works in the buyer's favour.

clue.text: Getting better, don't possibly include macho types

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters might be some other arrangement than the one shown
to include something is to take it inside, so one set of letters goes within the other

blocks.note: the word's letters, apostrophe dropped
he-men are muscular, macho men

explanation.surface: A recovering patient is told to avoid hanging around with tough guys.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in don't is ignored; only its four letters are mixed, and the macho men sit between the third and fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for recovering from illness, steadily improving in health.

clue.text: Drink ruined a nice hat

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spilt beverage has spoilt someone's smart headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is tea from China, such as lapsang souchong, a hot beverage.

clue.text: Talk too much about one buccaneer

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the first set of letters goes round the second

blocks.note: to prate is to chatter on foolishly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seafaring rogue is a terrible chatterbox.
explanation.walkthrough: PRATE goes round I: PR + I + ATE gives PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a sea robber of the Caribbean, so a pirate.

clue.text: Tomfoolery? Not for Civil Service leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their head, so only first letters count

blocks.note: to be anti something is to be against it, not for it
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Clowning around is frowned upon by the heads of government departments.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are foolish or playful capers, the same silly behaviour as tomfoolery.

clue.text: Oldies at dance left alone

indicators.note: dancing letters move around the floor and end up in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly people at a social dance were ignored and abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To be isolated is to be cut off from others, set apart or left on one's own.

clue.text: Type of shoe, in a manner of speaking

blocks.note: first meaning: a sturdy leather shoe with decorative punched holes
second meaning: a strong regional accent, especially Irish or Scottish

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' is a stock phrase meaning 'so to speak'; here it is a second meaning in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is both a heavy perforated shoe and a lilting regional accent, a way of pronouncing words.

clue.text: What agents do about gift

blocks.note: re is Latin for 'concerning', used as in business letters
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Talent agents fuss over the gifts they bring clients.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of a client, and acting for someone is to represent them.

clue.text: Wrong, or sure one's wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and must be put right

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Either you are mistaken, or the confident person is.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', joining fodder to indicator; the same word, wrong, serves once as definition and once as anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means containing an error, mistaken or incorrect.

clue.text: Unstretched? Not any more!

blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically: not made any longer in length
second meaning: the everyday phrase for something that has ceased

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the phrase literally into 'no' and 'longer', of something not lengthened.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard idiom for 'not any more', and taken literally it describes something not stretched out.

clue.text: Gourmets prepared to give us recipe

indicators.note: food that is prepared is chopped and mixed, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Food lovers are willing to share their cooking instructions with us.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of refined taste in food and drink, the same as a gourmet.

clue.text: Bird with Kelly hit on the head

blocks.note: a crow is a black bird
Ned Kelly was a famous nineteenth-century Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: Someone with a bird struck an outlaw on the skull.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelly needs a first name, and the best-known Kelly in crosswords is the bushranger Ned.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is informal slang for striking them on the top of the skull.

clue.text: Under fire, as nuts may be

definitions.note: describes nuts with their husks removed

blocks.note: first meaning: bombarded by artillery shells
second meaning: with the hard outer casing removed

explanation.walkthrough: A wartime meaning and a kitchen meaning share the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops under bombardment have been shelled, and nuts sold out of their husks are also described as shelled.

clue.text: Dubious about name for mixed drink

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the first word's letters wrap round the second

blocks.note: shady means of questionable honesty
n is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone is suspicious about what a cocktail is called.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a popular British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a blend of beer with lemonade or ginger beer, so a mixed beverage.

clue.text: Space — it could be germ-free

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests the letters may become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Outer space, perhaps, is a place without microbes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from bacteria and other contaminating microorganisms, as in surgery.

clue.text: Condemn poor scholar holding one back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so these letters are read from right to left
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a dunce is a slow or poor pupil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher criticises a weak student for keeping someone behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to publicly declare something wrong or evil, which is to condemn it.

clue.text: Phrase translated for mountain guide

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber needs an expression put into the local language for their guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people famed as guides and porters on Everest expeditions.

clue.text: Drug found in fishing vessel

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang name for heroin
second meaning: a small single-masted sailing boat used for fishing

explanation.surface: Narcotics are discovered aboard a trawler in a smuggling raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' sounds like a hidden-word signal, but it only links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Smack is street slang for heroin, and also the name of a traditional coastal fishing boat.

clue.text: Turning up with mother's cats

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother, here with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Mum's pets show up at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumas are large wild American felines, also called cougars or mountain lions.

clue.text: Slowly going round a sort of shed

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: lento is the musical direction for a slow tempo
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strolls lazily around a garden outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: Tempo markings in music are Italian words, and 'slowly' is one a solver should recognise.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or shelter whose roof rests against an existing wall.

clue.text: Heavy metal item damaged? Wait for delivery

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: lead is a famously heavy metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock fan's broken purchase means a long delay before a replacement arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests the music genre, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead time is the period between placing an order and receiving the goods, the wait a customer endures.

clue.text: Endlessly examine poker

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to study something is to examine it closely

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises a card game without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poker' could be a fireside iron, but it is the card game: stud is a form of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a variant in which some cards are dealt face up, often just called stud.

clue.text: Team thrills close friends

blocks.note: a side is a sports team
kicks are thrills, as in 'doing it for kicks'

explanation.surface: A sports team excites a bunch of loyal companions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a constant companion or assistant, a close friend who tags along.
